purpose: Convert the frozen X8 architecture into a coherent mass, thrust, propulsion-class, battery-series and ESC DC capability baseline suitable for continued product design.

change_control.rule: PB-02 inherits all PB-01 frozen decisions. Any change to a FROZEN decision requires PB-03 or an explicitly linked engineering change record; no silent overwrite is allowed.

inherited_pb01_decisions: controlled landing required after one motor/ESC loss
three independent high-voltage half-bridge gate-driver architecture
CAN-FD capable / Classic CAN compatible flight-controller interface
power-up/reset disarmed; no automatic re-arm after fault
3-phase BLDC/PMSM + two-level six-switch VSI + FOC/SVPWM capability

new_frozen_decisions.rationale: 85 kg is the controlled nominal design point centered in the already frozen 70-100 kg product payload envelope.

new_frozen_decisions.definition: Vehicle with propulsion, battery, structure, avionics and fixed mission hardware, excluding variable payload.
new_frozen_decisions.rationale: An 80 kg non-payload mass budget makes the 100 kg payload product a 180 kg MTOW-class vehicle while remaining close to current heavy-agriculture mass precedent. This is a mechanical/electrical co-design requirement, not a measured achieved mass.

new_frozen_decisions.meaning: Preliminary sizing treats each coaxial rotor's effective thrust as 85% of isolated-propeller bench thrust. The final vehicle must satisfy the frozen thrust requirements regardless of actual measured interaction.
new_frozen_decisions.rationale: Published coaxial-octocopter studies report roughly 12-16% hover thrust loss for representative coaxial configurations; 0.85 is a conservative product-sizing factor until our geometry is bench correlated.
Provides maneuver/control reserve above hover while avoiding sizing solely at laboratory maximum thrust.

At the PB-02 180 kg MTOW and 0.85 coaxial factor, normal hover requires 26.47 kgf isolated-equivalent per rotor, which fits the 27 kgf rated class. The 56-inch class saves about 10.8 kg across eight axes versus the X15 G2 63-inch benchmark while retaining adequate thrust reserve.

new_frozen_decisions.note: Controlled landing remains a vehicle-level requirement; these calculations establish thrust availability targets, not proof of controllability.

new_frozen_decisions.rationale: 18S supports the selected 45KV/56-inch propulsion class and remains below the inherited 80 V full-charge ceiling. Pack Ah/Wh and exact cell/pouch remain open until mission-energy closure.

Manufacturer 69 V X13 G2 curve places PB-02 max-MTOW hover near 44 A / 3.05 kW per isolated-equivalent axis, one-channel-loss landing near 54 A / 3.73 kW, and the 1.6 T/W point near 91 A / 6.26 kW. A 70 A continuous / 200 A 3 s DC capability preserves continuous degraded-landing margin and short-duration maneuver/fault reserve.
60 keRPM provides margin over the X13-class 45KV/42-pole manufacturer reference curve. Exact production motor remains open within the frozen propulsion performance class.

derived_reference_points_at_69v.source: Hobbywing X13 G2 MFP56x20 manufacturer load curve, interpolated only between published adjacent points

mass_budget_check.note: The remaining budget must cover battery, frame/arms, tank/pump/fixed mission hardware, avionics, landing gear and wiring. The individual allocations are still open and will be closed by mechanical/energy co-design.

still_open_after_pb02: battery mass, capacity, Wh and exact cell/pouch
exact rotor vertical spacing and arm geometry
exact 150 V MOSFET MPN and parallel count
current sensing, DC-link, precharge and thermal implementation
anti_hallucination_rule: PB-02 values are controlled engineering requirements and sizing factors. Manufacturer curve interpolation is not a claim that the custom coaxial vehicle has already achieved those electrical or aerodynamic results. Physical correlation is mandatory at later gates.
